plan.subject: Understand the fundamental concepts of classification, including its types, logistic regression, probabilistic interpretation, and optimization techniques.
plan.objective: Understand the fundamental concepts of classification, including its types, logistic regression, probabilistic interpretation, and optimization techniques.

blocks.title: What is Classification?
blocks.teachingObjective: Classification is a core supervised learning task that involves predicting discrete categories based on input data.
examples: Binary, multi-class, multi-label, and imbalanced classification tasks

blocks.title: Logistic Regression for Binary Classification
blocks.teachingObjective: Logistic regression is a foundational method for binary classification that models the probability of a class using a linear combination of features.
examples: Logistic regression models data by first creating a linear combination of features, then applying the logistic function

blocks.title: Probabilistic Interpretation of Logistic Regression
blocks.teachingObjective: The probabilistic interpretation provides a framework for understanding how logistic regression models class probabilities.
examples: P(Y=1|X=x) ≥ P(Y=0|X=x) defines the decision boundary for classification

blocks.title: Optimization and Convexity in Classification
blocks.teachingObjective: Understanding convexity and optimization is crucial for training classification models efficiently and avoiding local minima.
examples: The cost function for logistic regression is convex, ensuring that gradient descent converges to the global minimum
